inferred_links.I1: SecTime and BeatTime are binary64 members read by the 64-bit branch of the text conversion (spec: 'Double branch assumed'; review RVW-07 accepted).
inferred_links.I2: A conversion error while a nested value is read stops the open (as the transport-state-v1 refusals).
inferred_links.I3: Opening leaves markers and settings as the document gives them (spec A2): the read and the completion steps were checked statically (review RVW-01); two onset helpers, five indirect calls and the auto-warp trigger were not traced. Later self-made changes are excluded; cases 001 and 002 are controls.
inferred_links.I4: The sample length used by add_warp_marker is the duration in seconds of the clip's sample (0x1027b6954 source untraced). Cases keep at least 0.5 s from the 3 s length; case 024 holds in s, ms or frames.
inferred_links.I5: After its checks pass, an add or remove raises no further error (insert and delete pseudocode contain no throw; callees untraced).
inferred_links.I6: The marker lookup behaves as its corpus pseudocode reads (not dossier-confirmed).
inferred_links.I8: The conversions divide and multiply by the sample rate of the clip's sample (divisor source pseudocode).
inferred_links.I9: The macOS arm64 build computes the conversion, the rounding and the bounds as the x86_64 slice did (spec: same operation order; arm64 fmsub/fmadd and x86_64 glibc fma are both single-rounding).
inferred_links.I10: The first conversion call after opening uses the marker list held after opening (spec A3: the table is built once on first use; a build before the call would use the same list).
